output.content:
**Equinix xScale: AI-demand leasing read-through**

**Bottom line.** Equinix’s xScale business is its hyperscale offering, designed to let hyperscale customers place large “core” deployments alongside their Equinix IBX access points and interconnection ecosystems; management explicitly positions the combined xScale–IBX proposition for AI training-scale footprints and efficient inference connectivity. [[1]]

**Leasing momentum is strong.** In Q2 2026, Equinix signed 134 MW of xScale leasing across the Americas, while its current xScale portfolio had 604 MW leased, 577 MW operational, 23 operating facilities and 13 metros; the portfolio was shown as approximately 2,000 MW of eventual capacity and more than $23 billion of total investment when fully built out. [[2]]

**The near-term financial contribution was material but partly non-recurring.** The 134 MW of Q2 xScale leases included the Hampton transaction, generating approximately $120 million of non-recurring fees; Equinix reported Q2 revenue of $2.625 billion, up 16% year over year, and attributed part of that growth to one-time xScale fees. [[3]] [[4]]

**Underlying demand appears broader than that leasing-fee uplift.** Annualized gross bookings reached $424 million in Q2, and Equinix added a record 9,700 net interconnections; the company characterized bookings as broad-based, including emerging customer AI use cases. [[4]] [[2]]

**AI is an accelerant, rather than the sole demand driver.** Management’s Q3 2025 commentary referred to sustained demand for infrastructure and interconnection supporting both AI and non-AI workloads, while the Q2 2026 release highlighted expanded Cisco/NVIDIA collaboration intended to accelerate enterprise AI deployments across Equinix’s global footprint. [[5]] [[4]]

**Why xScale is strategically important.** The program extends Equinix from retail colocation and interconnection into large hyperscale campuses, while retaining a differentiated connection to its IBX footprint; Equinix’s investor materials reported 282 data centers, 77 markets, 36 countries, 230 cloud on-ramps and 522,000+ interconnections as of Q2 2026. [[2]]

**Capital availability supports expansion.** Equinix’s U.S. JV with GIC and CPP Investments is intended to raise more than $15 billion including debt, build multiple greater-than-100-MW campuses, and add more than 1.5 GW of hyperscale capacity over time; Equinix holds a 25% equity interest while GIC and CPP each hold 37.5%. [[6]]

**Implications for investors.** The 134-MW quarter and pre-leased expansion capacity support the view that AI and cloud customers are converting demand into large commitments, and Equinix said a significant portion of its remaining 2026 capacity additions was already committed through bookings and presales. [[2]] [[7]]

**Key caveat.** Investors should separate recurring operating growth from episodic xScale transaction fees: Equinix reported that Q2 adjusted-EBITDA margin expanded 300 basis points year over year, but approximately 150 basis points of expansion remained after excluding xScale leasing fees. [[2]]

**Forward view.** Equinix raised 2026 revenue-growth guidance to 11%–12% and, as of the latest reported quarter ended June 30, 2026, was accelerating more than 7,000 cabinets originally planned for 2027 into Q4 2026, signaling confidence that demand can absorb earlier delivered capacity. [[2]] [[4]]
